reference.method: integer median closed form; damped Newton at 50 digits on the README log density, from the fitted values

not_refined.location: closed form or exhaustive enumeration (independently checked)

global.statement: For a nonconstant integer sample with both coefficients free, a finite MLE exists. Every integer in the sample median interval maximizes location, with the same unique scale. Location is unique exactly when that interval contains one integer. Constant samples have only an unattained point-mass supremum. With integer location held, a unique interior scale MLE exists unless all observations equal that location. With scale held strictly between zero and one, the integer medians maximize location even for constant samples. Holding both coefficients leaves likelihood evaluation.
global.reason: Writing $p=b$ and $d=n^{-1}\sum_i|x_i-\mu|$, the log likelihood per observation is $\log(1-p)-\log(1+p)+d\log p$. Since $\log p<0$, location maximization is exactly absolute-deviation minimization over the integers. For $d>0$, the scale score vanishes exactly when $d(1-p^2)=2p$, giving the unique maximizer $p=d/(\sqrt{1+d^2}+1)$. For $d=0$, the likelihood decreases strictly in $p$ and approaches its supremum only as $p\to0$.

integer_enumeration.argument: absolute-deviation convexity; all integer medians maximize
